questions.title: Square List Comprehension Drill
questions.description:
Pure construct drill: build the squares of the first n positive integers with a single list comprehension and print the resulting list.

Input Format:
One line with the integer n.

Output Format:
Print the list of squares from 1*1 to n*n, exactly as Python prints a list.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 20
questions.sourcecode:
n = int(input())
print([i * i for i in range(1, n + 1)])

questions.title: Even Only Comprehension Drill
questions.description:
Pure construct drill: read a list of integers and keep only the even ones using a conditional list comprehension (an if clause after the for clause).

Input Format:
One line with integers separated by spaces.

Output Format:
Print the list of even values in input order, exactly as Python prints a list.

Constraints:
1 <= count <= 50, -1000 <= value <= 1000
questions.sourcecode:
nums = [int(x) for x in input().split()]
print([x for x in nums if x % 2 == 0])

questions.title: Uppercase Words Comprehension Drill
questions.description:
Pure construct drill: transform every word in the input to upper case using a list comprehension over the words.

Input Format:
One line with words separated by spaces.

Output Format:
Print the list of upper-cased words in input order, exactly as Python prints a list.

Constraints:
1 <= words <= 20, each word has length 1 to 20
questions.sourcecode:
words = input().split()
print([w.upper() for w in words])

questions.title: Word Length Dict Comprehension Drill
questions.description:
Pure construct drill: build a dictionary mapping each word to its length with a dictionary comprehension and print it. Duplicate words collapse to one entry.

Input Format:
One line with words separated by spaces.

Output Format:
Print the dictionary exactly as Python prints it.

Constraints:
1 <= words <= 15, each word has length 1 to 12
questions.sourcecode:
words = input().split()
print({w: len(w) for w in words})

questions.title: First Letter Set Comprehension Drill
questions.description:
Pure construct drill: collect the first letter of every word with a set comprehension, then print the letters sorted (a set itself must never be printed directly).

Input Format:
One line with lowercase words separated by spaces.

Output Format:
Print the sorted list of distinct first letters, exactly as Python prints a list.

Constraints:
1 <= words <= 30, each word has length 1 to 15, lowercase letters only
questions.sourcecode:
words = input().split()
print(sorted({w[0] for w in words}))

questions.title: Matrix Flatten Comprehension Drill
questions.description:
Pure construct drill: read a matrix and flatten it row by row with a single nested list comprehension (two for clauses in one comprehension).

Input Format:
Line 1: r and c separated by a space.
Lines 2..r+1: each row with c integers separated by spaces.

Output Format:
Print the flattened list in row-major order, exactly as Python prints a list.

Constraints:
1 <= r, c <= 10, -100 <= value <= 100
questions.sourcecode:
r, c = map(int, input().split())
grid = [[int(x) for x in input().split()] for _ in range(r)]
print([x for row in grid for x in row])

questions.title: GST Price List Comprehension
questions.description:
A shop terminal recomputes its shelf prices with 18% GST in one sweep. Read the base prices and build the final prices with a single list comprehension multiplying each price by 1.18, then print them.

Input Format:
One line with base prices separated by spaces.

Output Format:
Print the prices after GST, each formatted to exactly 2 decimal places, space separated, in input order.

Constraints:
1 <= count <= 20, 0 <= price <= 100000
questions.sourcecode:
prices = [float(x) for x in input().split()]
with_gst = [p * 1.18 for p in prices]
print(" ".join(f"{p:.2f}" for p in with_gst))

questions.title: Passing Students Filter Comprehension
questions.description:
A teacher posts results: build the list of students who scored at least 50 using one conditional list comprehension over the name/score pairs, then join the names for the notice board. If nobody passed, print None.

Input Format:
Line 1: the student names separated by spaces.
Line 2: the scores separated by spaces, aligned with the names.

Output Format:
Print the passing names in input order, joined with ", " (comma and space), or None when the list is empty.

Constraints:
1 <= students <= 30, 0 <= score <= 100, names are distinct
questions.sourcecode:
names = input().split()
scores = [int(x) for x in input().split()]
passed = [name for name, score in zip(names, scores) if score >= 50]
print(", ".join(passed) if passed else "None")

questions.title: Tag Dedupe Set Comprehension
questions.description:
A blog backend normalizes the tag cloud of an article: collect the distinct tags with a set comprehension and publish them in alphabetical order (sorted, since sets are unordered).

Input Format:
One line with lowercase tags separated by spaces.

Output Format:
Print the distinct tags in alphabetical order, space separated.

Constraints:
1 <= tags <= 40, each tag has length 1 to 12, lowercase letters only
questions.sourcecode:
tags = input().split()
print(" ".join(sorted({t for t in tags})))

questions.title: Seat Grid Reservation Flatten
questions.description:
A theatre reservation sheet stores seats as a grid of seat codes. Flatten the grid into the single display row of codes using a nested comprehension over the rows and codes.

Input Format:
Line 1: r and c separated by a space.
Lines 2..r+1: each row with c seat codes separated by spaces.

Output Format:
Print all codes in row-major order, space separated.

Constraints:
1 <= r, c <= 8, each code has length 1 to 3
questions.sampleinput1:
2 3
A1 A2 A3
B1 B2 B3
questions.sampleoutput1: A1 A2 A3 B1 B2 B3
questions.sourcecode:
r, c = map(int, input().split())
grid = [input().split() for _ in range(r)]
print(" ".join(code for row in grid for code in row))

questions.title: Even Sensor Calibration Comp
questions.description:
A sensor gateway calibrates its stream in one pass: every even reading is doubled and odd readings are dropped. Build the calibrated values with a single conditional list comprehension (no .append, no map, no filter).

Input Format:
Line 1: the integer n.
Line 2: n integers separated by spaces.

Output Format:
Print the doubled even values in input order, space separated; if no value survives, print None.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100, -10000 <= value <= 10000
questions.sourcecode:
n = int(input())
values = [int(x) for x in input().split()]
calibrated = [v * 2 for v in values if v % 2 == 0]
print(" ".join(str(v) for v in calibrated) if calibrated else "None")

questions.title: Threshold Verdict Else Comprehension
questions.description:
An exam scanner stamps every score with a verdict in one comprehension using an if/else expression (P when the score is at least the threshold, F otherwise), then reports the pass and fail totals.

Input Format:
Line 1: the threshold t.
Line 2: the integer n.
Line 3: n scores separated by spaces.

Output Format:
Line 1: the verdict letters in input order, space separated.
Line 2: pass X fail Y where X and Y are the two counts.

Constraints:
0 <= t <= 200, 1 <= n <= 100, -100 <= score <= 200
questions.sampleoutput1:
P F P P
pass 3 fail 1
questions.output3:
F P P F P
pass 3 fail 2
questions.sourcecode:
t = int(input())
n = int(input())
values = [int(x) for x in input().split()]
verdicts = ["P" if v >= t else "F" for v in values]
passes = len([v for v in values if v >= t])
print(" ".join(verdicts))
print(f"pass {passes} fail {n - passes}")

questions.title: Badge Roster Inversion Comp
questions.description:
A badge system keeps staff as name -> badge number and needs the inverse lookup table badge -> name, built with a dictionary comprehension. When two people share a badge, the person processed later owns it - but the badge keeps the position of its first occurrence. Print the inverted table in that order.

Input Format:
Line 1: the integer n.
Lines 2..n+1: one entry per line: name and badge number separated by a space.

Output Format:
One line per distinct badge, in first-occurrence order: the badge number, a space, the owning name.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 50, name length 1 to 15, 1 <= badge <= 9999

questions.title: Remainder Bucket Set Comp
questions.description:
A hash-sharding tool studies which buckets a batch of keys lands in. Collect the distinct remainders value mod k with a set comprehension (no .add, no set() constructor), then report them sorted together with the bucket count.

Input Format:
Line 1: n and k separated by a space.
Line 2: n integers separated by spaces.

Output Format:
Line 1: the distinct remainders in increasing order, space separated.
Line 2: how many distinct remainders there are.

Constraints:
1 <= k <= 100, 1 <= n <= 200, -10000 <= value <= 10000
questions.sourcecode:
n, k = map(int, input().split())
values = [int(x) for x in input().split()]
remainders = {v % k for v in values}
print(" ".join(str(r) for r in sorted(remainders)))
print(len(remainders))

questions.title: Transpose Grid Nested Comp
questions.description:
A spreadsheet exporter needs the transpose of a numeric grid. Build it with a nested list comprehension (no .append, no zip): the outer comprehension walks the column indices, the inner one gathers each column.

Input Format:
Line 1: r and c separated by a space.
Lines 2..r+1: each row with c integers separated by spaces.

Output Format:
Print c lines: row j of the transposed matrix, values space separated.

Constraints:
1 <= r, c <= 10, -99 <= value <= 99
questions.sourcecode:
r, c = map(int, input().split())
grid = [[int(x) for x in input().split()] for _ in range(r)]
transposed = [[grid[i][j] for i in range(r)] for j in range(c)]
for row in transposed:
    print(" ".join(str(v) for v in row))

questions.title: Freezer Restock Dict Comp
questions.description:
A freezer kitchen flags everything below the restock threshold. Build the low-stock table with a dictionary comprehension over the name/qty pairs keeping only quantities strictly below the threshold, then print it in insertion order. If nothing is low, print All stocked.

Input Format:
Line 1: the integer n.
Line 2: the threshold t.
Lines 3..n+2: one item per line: name and quantity separated by a space.

Output Format:
One line per low item in input order: the name, a space, the quantity. Or the single line All stocked.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 50, item names are distinct, 0 <= qty <= 500, 1 <= t <= 500

questions.title: Analytics Grid Dashboard
questions.description:
A metrics dashboard renders a numeric grid entirely with comprehensions: row totals, column totals and the grand total. Build every aggregate with comprehensions only - no .append, no map, no filter. Row totals come from one comprehension over the rows; column totals from a nested comprehension that walks each column index.

Input Format:
Line 1: r and c separated by a space.
Lines 2..r+1: each row with c integers separated by spaces.

Output Format:
Line 1: the r row totals, space separated.
Line 2: the c column totals, space separated.
Line 3: the grand total.

Constraints:
1 <= r, c <= 10, -100 <= value <= 100
questions.sourcecode:
r, c = [int(x) for x in input().split()]
grid = [[int(x) for x in input().split()] for _ in range(r)]
row_sums = [sum(row) for row in grid]
col_sums = [sum(grid[i][j] for i in range(r)) for j in range(c)]
print(" ".join(str(s) for s in row_sums))
print(" ".join(str(s) for s in col_sums))
print(sum(row_sums))

questions.title: Run Length Compression Report
questions.description:
A telemetry linker compresses repeated symbols before transmission. Given a string, produce its run-length report: every maximal run of equal characters becomes one line with the character and its count. Build the runs with comprehensions only (no .append, no itertools.groupby): first collect the indices where a new run starts, then pair each start with its run length in a second comprehension.

Input Format:
One line with the string (lowercase letters only, no spaces).

Output Format:
One line per run, in order: the character, a space, its count.

Constraints:
1 <= len(s) <= 1000, lowercase letters only
questions.sourcecode:
s = input().strip()
starts = [0] + [i for i in range(1, len(s)) if s[i] != s[i - 1]]
pairs = [[s[i], (starts[j + 1] if j + 1 < len(starts) else len(s)) - i] for j, i in enumerate(starts)]
for ch, cnt in pairs:
    print(ch, cnt)

questions.title: Warehouse Inventory Diff Report
questions.description:
A retail chain compares its warehouse stock with a store's stock. Read both inventories into dicts built by dictionary comprehensions (no dict() constructor, no .append), then report: the items that exist only in the warehouse (alphabetical, comma separated, or None), the items present in both whose quantity changed (alphabetical, one per line as the item and its signed change store minus warehouse), and the net change across those common items.

Input Format:
Line 1: the integer n.
Lines 2..n+1: warehouse entries: item and quantity separated by a space.
Line n+2: the integer m.
Lines n+3..n+m+2: store entries: item and quantity separated by a space.

Output Format:
Line 1: warehouse-only items alphabetically joined with ", ", or None.
Then one line per changed common item, alphabetically: item delta (e.g. bolt -10).
Last line: net X where X is the sum of the deltas.

Constraints:
1 <= n, m <= 40, item names are distinct within each list, name length 1 to 12, 0 <= qty <= 10000

questions.title: Defect Bucket Matrix Comp
questions.description:
A factory quality line sorts defect scores into four buckets: Low 0-39, Medium 40-69, High 70-89 and Critical 90-100. Build a 4-row membership matrix with a nested comprehension that uses an if/else expression - row i has a 1 in column j exactly when score j belongs to bucket i - then print each row and each bucket's total. No .append and no map allowed.

Input Format:
Line 1: the integer n.
Line 2: n defect scores separated by spaces.

Output Format:
Four lines: the membership rows for Low, Medium, High, Critical, values space separated.
Then one line: L:x M:y H:z C:w with the four bucket totals.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100, 0 <= score <= 100
questions.sourcecode:
n = int(input())
scores = [int(x) for x in input().split()]
bounds = [(0, 39), (40, 69), (70, 89), (90, 100)]
matrix = [[1 if lo <= s <= hi else 0 for s in scores] for lo, hi in bounds]
for row in matrix:
    print(" ".join(str(v) for v in row))
labels = ["L", "M", "H", "C"]
totals = [sum(row) for row in matrix]
print(" ".join(f"{lab}:{t}" for lab, t in zip(labels, totals)))
